newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha gains ground in slim trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha gains ground in slim trade.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were notionally higher in slim Wednesday trading, tracking overnight crude gains, traders said.
Most naphtha traders were relaxed with holidays lined up later in the week and early next week in Japan as well as other Asian trading centres, they added.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half July was nominally assessed at $209.00/211.00, up from late Monday's $208.50/209.50.
The Tokyo market was closed on Tuesday for a national holiday.

Contango in near-term naphtha spreads widened, with second-half June/second-half July quoted at minus $2.50/minus $1.50. Late last week, the second-half June contract was valued only 25 to 50 cents lower than second-half July.
Traders said several European cargoes in the region that remained unsold dampened sentiment for near-term cargoes.

In low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) trading, requirements from Japan are expected to pick up in May due to spring turnarounds, fuel oil traders said. Some other traders said, however, May demand will not be much different from April or March due to high domestic stocks. -- Tokyo Energy Desk
